_comment: Recipe A is the permissions block. Recipe B is the hooks block. Copy ONE of
them into .claude/settings.json at the repository root, then replace every
MODULE-YOU-ARE-NOT-TOUCHING with a module your plan puts out of scope.
The leading single slash anchors a path rule to the directory the session
was started in. Start the agent at the repository root (SETUP.md step 6)
and that is the repository root. No leading slash means relative to the
working directory, and a double slash means the filesystem root.
Write the rules on Edit, not on Write. Path rules are only consulted for Edit
and Read. An Edit rule already covers Write and NotebookEdit.
Settings and hooks reload when you save the file, so there is nothing to
restart. Check that yours was picked up: run /status and read the Setting
sources line. A file with broken JSON (often a stray trailing comma from
hand copying this block) is skipped, silently mid-session, and the next
session start shows a Settings Error. Absent from that line means the
The hook runs through a shell wrapper on purpose. Only exit code 2 blocks a
tool call. Exit 1 is treated as a broken hook and the edit proceeds. A typo
in protect.py is a syntax error, which exits 1 before any of its own code
can run. The wrapper turns every non-zero exit into a 2.
